description: DecoderPro's id, formatted from the key: road_name, a space, road_number (CSX 2121). bin/cars, new_locos.json and the cards read it. locos.loco_roster_id in ops/hart-ops/card_pipeline/locos.py formats it, and locos.ops_id formats the Operations Pro id (road_name and road_number with nothing between: CSX2121). tools/ops/check_locos.py fails a roster_id that is not the formatted pair, and holds both engine rosters and the train list to the master.
The road name as the rosters give it (BO, CR, CSX), not the display form on a card (B&O). With road_number, the row's key.
The road number, as text: NWR 06 keeps its leading zero. With road_name, the row's key.
The DCC address. Required only when bin/cars locos publish sends the loco to DecoderPro; for the locos it already has, the DecoderPro roster on the Pi holds it.
yes for a long (four-figure) address. Empty: publish decides from the address (over 127 is long).
The builder (EMD, GE, ALCO). Empty: the cards take it from the model (engine_lookup.manufacturer_for_model).
The model as Operations Pro names it (GP38, SW1200).
Diesel, Steam or Electric: the Operations Pro engine type.
Length in scale feet, as the engine roster gives it.
Weight in tons, as the engine roster gives it.
yes when the decoder has sound.
The loco's photo in the car-card intake (IMG_9181.png, or an intake file name). The cards and the public gallery read it; the gallery adds a photo only once.
Free text. publish sends it to DecoderPro as the entry's comment. A value that is the working answer to an owner question says so here.
